key_insight: TT-SCHA computes binary-alloy crystal free energies without random sampling, matching molecular dynamics within 0.13 meV per atom at 600–1000 K.
engineering_relevance: The method offers efficient thermodynamic evaluation of ordered alloys, using 420–500 times fewer core-seconds per run than the molecular-dynamics benchmark.
method: Model B2 NiAl and gamma-TiAl with embedded-atom potentials.
Apply a self-consistent harmonic approximation corrected to third order in temperature.
Evaluate thermal averages using tensor-train integrals over one atom and its neighbors.
evidence_signal: Validation used 65,536-atom molecular dynamics and same-potential published results, with gamma-TiAl elastic constants agreeing within 1 GPa and thermal expansion within 0.012 percentage points.
watch_item: Sampling error is absent, but interpolation starting pivots introduce numerical variability of up to 9 MPa in pressure, reduced by averaging three runs.
paper_title: TT-SCHA for Thermodynamics of Binary Alloys
